findings.title: Cyberattack wipes cloud data at major Russian hosting provider Beget
findings.summary_md: Beget, one of Russia's largest domain registrars and hosting companies, said attackers accessed the systems used to manage its infrastructure and ran scripts designed to erase data after an overnight attack on November 2, 2026. The damage was severe in its cloud infrastructure, where data tied to virtual private servers, cloud storage, and Kubernetes services was wiped, and the company said it lost all binary backups of virtual servers while file-level backups stayed intact. Beget said restoring all services would take considerable time because more than 1,000 servers had to be manually inspected.

findings.title: Cyberattack Disrupts Russian Web Hosting Provider ESTT
findings.summary_md: Russian hosting provider ESTT said a cyberattack using file-encrypting malware disrupted services across its cloud infrastructure on Sunday, November 8, 2026. By Monday it had restored 90 percent of customers' virtual servers, though customers still could not access account dashboards, and the company said it found no evidence of a customer data leak. The article ties the hit to the Nov. 2 Beget outage, which RBC reported affected around 500,000 online resources including government service websites, news outlets, and online stores.

findings.title: Russian cloud firm Beget rebuilds from scratch after data wiper attack
findings.summary_md: Beget, a Russian hosting, cloud, and domain provider serving more than 200,000 customers, is rebuilding its cloud infrastructure from scratch after a wiper attack on the night of November 1, 2026 reached the management layer of its entire architecture and ran data-zeroing scripts. The company disconnected all servers from the network shortly after detecting the malware, and said cloud data across VPS, S3, and Kubernetes was lost along with CDN settings and IP configurations. A November 6 assessment stated VPS file backups would be available for only about half of VPS users, and roughly 1,000 servers required manual checks for vulnerabilities and hidden scripts before being returned to service.

findings.title: Belarusian cloud provider ActiveCloud reported a serious outage due to a cyberattack
findings.summary_md: The earliest ActiveCloud report located: the company said a massive cyberattack recorded at 03:30 AM on November 10, 2026 left many services and communication channels unavailable, citing Office Life. The ActiveCloud website was not opening, and chats, telephony, and the ticketing system used for customer support inside client accounts were down. Numerous corporate resources, programs, and websites are hosted on ActiveCloud (Active Technologies) cloud services, and the company also offers cloud solution development and information security services.

findings.title: Belarusian Provider ActiveCloud Targeted in Cyberattack
findings.summary_md: REFORM.news reported overnight on November 10, 2026 that Belarusian hosting and cloud provider ActiveCloud was hit by a serious cyberattack. According to the company, its secure cloud hosting service in Belarus, its email service in Belarus and Russia, and the ActiveCloud website all suffered disruptions. Customer support channels, including chats, telephone support, and the ticketing system, were also unavailable while the company worked to mitigate the consequences.
